title: Affinity-driven, entropy-aware canary routing with throttled fallbacks
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Background: We need a deterministic, low-latency routing layer that preserves per-session/model-version affinity during gradual rollouts (canary/A-B), while ensuring traffic is automatically degraded to compatible variants when capacity or region constraints occur. Current approaches either shove all affinity into session pins (causing hot spots) or do naive probabilistic canaries that ignore regional cost/tier preferences and model compatibility.

Problem statement: Design a routing policy that: 1) honors version pinning for session affinity where required; 2) respects region and tier policy (hosted/dedicated/private) and canary percentage; 3) throttles novel variant assignment in high-entropy sessions to avoid increased tail latency and burst capacity spikes; and 4) specifies a deterministic fallback path to quantized/compat model variants when the preferred variant is unavailable.

Goals:
- Provide predictable per-session model-version affinity with bounded state (TTL-based).
- Make canary/A-B assignment both deterministic (for traceability) and entropy-aware (to avoid splitting sessions that will generate high compute).
- Integrate cost/latency tiering so that requests in a low-cost tier are not silently routed to high-cost dedicated capacity unless policy allows.
- Expose telemetry and guards so SRE/PM can abort or throttle canaries fast.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Strong affinity increases cache/KV reuse and lowers latency but causes hot keys; we must cap concurrent pinned sessions per model variant.
- Strict compatibility checks (model architecture/quantization) during fallback add lookup cost; we will cache compatibility maps.
- Deterministic assignment requires a seeded hash; seed rotation for privacy must be supported.

High-level approach:
1) Session representation: each session has (session_id, entropy_score, regional_hint, requested_tier, user_flags). Entropy_score is estimated from recent token rate and average sequence length (computed by Console telemetry).
2) Assignment pipeline:
   - Step A: Evaluate policy (region -> tier -> customer constraints). If policy disallows requested tier in region, map to allowed tier list.
   - Step B: If session is already pinned (session_pin table), return pinned variant if healthy. Pins have TTL (default 12h) and a max-concurrency soft cap.
   - Step C: If unpinned, compute deterministic canary bucket using H = HMAC(seed, session_id) -> bucket in [0,1). For A-B or canary, compare bucket to rollout_percentage.
   - Step D: Entropy-throttle: if entropy_score > threshold_for_variant and current_allocated_for_variant > concurrency_threshold, force fallback to lower-cost compatible variant or queue into warm pool.
   - Step E: Fallback resolution: consult compatibility_map[preferred_variant] -> ordered list of compatible variants (same arch > quantized > distilled). Choose first healthy candidate in ordered list that respects tier/region.
   - Step F: Record final assignment in routing_trace and optionally create a session_pin if policy/flags permit.

Pseudocode (simplified):

 assign(session):
   policy = resolve_policy(session.regional_hint, session.requested_tier, customer_rules)
   if session_pin.exists(session.id):
     v = session_pin.get(session.id)
     if healthy(v): return v
   bucket = HMAC(seed, session.id) % 10000 / 10000.0
   if bucket < rollout_pct(preferred_variant) and session.applies_to_canary:
     candidate = preferred_variant
   else:
     candidate = stable_variant
   if session.entropy_score > variant.entropy_capacity_threshold and variant.current_alloc > variant.concurrent_soft_cap:
     candidate = next_compatible_lower_cost(candidate, policy.allowed_tiers)
   candidate = fallback_lookup(candidate, policy.allowed_regions)
   record_routing_trace(session.id, candidate)
   if should_pin(session, candidate): session_pin.set(session.id, candidate, ttl=12h)
   return candidate


Observability and controls:
- Expose per-variant counters: active_pinned_sessions, entropy_prone_rejections, fallback_rate, avg_latency_by_pin_state.
- Console controls: throttle canary by reducing rollout_pct and by toggling entropy_throttle_enabled.
- Alert rules: fallback_rate > 3% for 5m; entropy_throttle_rejections spike; per-variant pinned_session_count > 95th percentile.

API/Schema changes:
- routing.policy v2 will add fields: allow_pin (bool), pin_ttl_seconds, entropy_throttle_threshold, entropy_concurrency_cap, compatibility_precedence (list).
- session_pin store schema: session_id, variant_key, created_at, expires_at, pinned_by (route/policy).

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for deterministic bucket assignment and seed rotation invariants.
- Integration test that stubs high-entropy session patterns and verifies throttling goes to fallback variant.
- Canary smoke: deploy to non-prod region with synthetic sessions that vary entropy and verify telemetry.
- Load test: ensure pin store handles 1M pins with TTL expiration and does not cause hot partitions.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 1 (dev): feature behind flag in router; deterministic behavior only, no pins created.
- Phase 2 (staged): enable pinning for 1% of sessions for a single small customer; monitor pinned_session_count and latency.
- Phase 3 (gradual): open to % by project and allow SRE to increase rollout_pct; default entropy_throttle_enabled = true.
- Kill-switch: global flag to disable all canary assignment (fall back to stable).
acceptance_criteria: Router can deterministically assign sessions to canary or stable variants using seeded hashing and records trace IDs.
Entropy-throttle prevents assignment to canary variant when session entropy and variant concurrency exceed configured thresholds (configurable per-variant).
Fallback path selects a compatible variant that respects region and tier policies and is marked healthy by the health-check system.
Session pins are recorded with TTL and do not exceed per-variant soft caps; pins expire correctly and are evicted under pressure.
Console exposes metrics: pinned_sessions, entropy_rejections, fallback_rate and allows toggling entropy_throttle and adjusting rollout_pct.
Integration and load tests validate correctness and that the pin store scales without hot partitions.
decisions: Use seeded HMAC(session_id, global_seed) for deterministic bucket assignment to ensure reproducibility across routers.
Make entropy_score a first-class signal computed from recent tokens/sec and avg_seq_len and propagated in the routing request header.
Implement compatibility_map as a cached, monotonic list per-variant: [exact, quantized, distilled, api_compatible_stub].
Default pin TTL = 12 hours; allow per-policy override down to 30 minutes for high-turnover canaries.
Enforce a configurable soft cap on pinned sessions per variant; exceeders are routed to fallback without creating extra pins.
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Drafted design and pseudocode; aligned with PM on goals and constraints.
2026-03-11: Spike completed to measure entropy signal feasibility in telemetry; prototype entropy estimator returns stable scores for synthetic workloads.
2026-03-12: Reviewed with SRE and Runtime; SRE requested evict-on-pressure guarantee and eviction metrics which were added to acceptance criteria.
notes: Open questions: Should pin creation be conditional on user_tier (e.g., enterprise customers always get pins)? How to rotate global seed without violating existing pins - proposed: dual-hash on rotation window and backfill pins if necessary. Need follow-up with Privacy to confirm seed rotation policy.
